I farm 20 mu, and with wheat-maize on the same land, I will run the full 20 mu through both crops. I finished 20 years in the field, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked before in Quzhou. Around here, if water is available from the well, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a bit of input. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more fertilizer at the base, water about three times, and keep the stand steady through winter and spring. For maize, I will go with hybrid seed, keep the land turning fast after wheat, mostly no-tillage if the straw handling is fine, then push nitrogen a bit because maize responds clearly when water can follow. I will not go too light on pesticide either, because once disease, aphids, armyworm, or rust gets ahead, it costs more to fix. I also have some family labor going off-farm, so I will keep the plan practical and efficient, not something that needs too many extra passes.
